source.title: Partitioned integrators for thermodynamic parameterization of neural networks
source.authors: B. Leimkuhler; Charles Matthews; Tiffany J. Vlaar

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; no apparent garbling or truncation.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer performance on held-out classification data using different datasets and settings from the optimizer claim’s cited benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. on random-label memorization but does not test random labels. Its own optimizer comparisons on spiral and trigonometric classification data bear on V4. Its statements about overfitting and parameter distributions do not test the other listed versions.
record.test_reason: Direct Adam–SGD comparisons measure held-out classification accuracy in a new setting: synthetic planar data and single-hidden-layer networks. They bear on the scope of V4, although they do not reproduce its image or language benchmarks or establish a generalization difference at matched training performance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report faster convergence and improved test accuracy on challenging spiral and trigonometric tasks, competitive performance without significant gains on MNIST, and reduced variability or overfitting under suitable parameter choices. They explicitly do not claim universal protection against overfitting and call for testing on deep networks and large-scale benchmarks.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares Adam and SGD with Langevin-based methods on synthetic planar classification tasks and MNIST using single-hidden-layer perceptrons; it does not reproduce the cited optimizer benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset complexity, training step, initialization, temperature, additive-noise strength, friction, stepsize, and training-data amount affect reported performance.

fits_no_version.finding: On harder trigonometric data, Adam remains around 73% test accuracy after 100000 steps, below LOL and AdLaLa.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Partitioned thermodynamic training methods can outperform Adam on challenging synthetic classification tasks.

record.problems: The optimizer comparisons focus on single-hidden-layer networks and a limited collection of toy planar datasets. Hyperparameter tuning was not equally broad across methods: for the Figure 10 comparison the authors varied Adam’s stepsize but retained its default decay rates. Most runs do not report uncertainty; figures contain additional results whose exact values are not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 7 reports test accuracies for SGD and Adam on four-turn spirals at steps 50, 1000 and 10k, but these are not extracted because the caption groups several optimizer results in a compact sequence and the figure's text does not provide a direct Adam-versus-SGD comparison for each stage. Figure 14 shows mean and variance curves without numerical values; precise figure-only values were not extracted.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label fitting or comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or intervention on local connectivity.

No direct Adam–SGD comparison on image or language benchmarks; no matched-training-performance analysis, momentum-SGD comparison, decay-schedule tuning, broad optimizer tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, or word-level language-model experiment.
No controlled large-batch comparison under fixed epoch budgets or tests of adaptations that remove its penalty.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation measure or ranking of generalization gaps against norm and margin measures.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining comparison.

missing.what: Figure 10 contains direct Adam and SGD test-accuracy results across learning rates after 37500 steps on four-turn spirals. These are relevant to V4's limited-tuning comparison but are absent from the rows and not declared in rows_left_out; numerical values require the figure.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Synthetic-task reversals qualify V4's scope rather than refute its stated image and language benchmark finding. The record's support labels for R8 and R10 are invalid. Figure 7's omitted comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out random-label evaluation.
No width sweep around the zero-training-error threshold.
Only fully connected single-hidden-layer networks are studied; no convolutional comparison.
Does not test image-classification or language benchmarks, momentum SGD, broad hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, or word-level language models.
No large-batch comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- or margin-based measures.
Does not identify and remove memorized training examples.

rows.note: Adam test accuracy is slightly below SGD at this reported step.

rows.subject: 20-node SHLP trained with Adam
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the two-turn spiral dataset; reported mean test accuracy across runs.
rows.note: The text describes the variance comparison but gives no mean accuracy values by optimizer.
rows.check: The supplied figure text does not preserve readable mean curves. The comparison also uses standard PyTorch initialization for this Adam condition but Gaussian initialization for SGD; the figure includes a separate Gaussian-initialized Adam condition.

rows.subject: 20-node SHLP trained with Adam
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the four-turn spiral dataset; test accuracy compared with other optimizers.
rows.baseline: AdLaLa and LOL reached higher accuracy; exact values not stated in text
rows.note: The authors state Adam's maximum test accuracy remained around 73% after 100,000 steps.
rows.check: Misidentified experiment: Figure 12 uses trigonometric data with a=10 and a 100-node SHLP, not four-turn spirals and 20 nodes. The roughly 73% Adam result is compared with the authors' LOL and AdLaLa methods, not SGD; it cannot establish V4.

relationships.reason: R1–R2 show only a small SGD advantage, 66% versus 65%, at an early checkpoint without uncertainty.
relationships.display_finding: Reported SGD accuracy of 66% versus Adam's 65% remains unverified and lacks uncertainty estimates.

relationships.reason: R3–R6 show Adam outperforming SGD, 89% versus 66% and 99% versus 96%, extending the conditions where the usual SGD advantage does not appear.
relationships.display_finding: Reported Adam accuracy advantages at both later checkpoints remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Two-turn spirals, 20-node SHLP, 100-run averages after 10000 steps
relationships.reason: R7–R8 report Adam at 83.7% versus SGD at 79%; this synthetic setting favors Adam.
relationships.display_finding: Reported average Adam accuracy of 83.7% versus SGD's 79% remains unverified.
